names.form: Sfântul Ierarh Iosif de Alaverdi, Georgia

names.note: Read out of «Св. Јосиф еп. Алавердски.» in this folder’s Serbian citation.
Read out of saint.gr's page for 7 Μαΐου, which heads him «Οσιος Ιωσηφ Μαθητης Του Οσιου Ιωαννη», with the rank words and the clause about his teacher left off.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 15 сентября ст. ст. — «Свт. Иосифа, еп. Алавердского (570) (Груз.)»
doxologia.ro, 15 septembrie — „Sfântul Ierarh Iosif de Alaverdi, Georgia”
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Ιωάννης και οι μαθητές αυτού»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps the company, and it is plainly the same company: John out of Syria and the twelve chosen to go into Iberia, whose names the page prints as «Σίω, Δαβίδ, Αντώνιος, Θαδδαίος, Στέφανος, Ισήδωρος, Μιχαήλ, Πύρρος, Ζήνων, Ισέ, Ιωσήφ και Άβιβος». **Thirteen head lines, thirteen names, so thirteen folders**, and the corpus already holds every one of them, so the whole company is upgrades and no folder is created. **`shio-of-mgvime` is the one exception and is not touched**: its `greek` row is already `venerated`, on 4 Φεβρουαρίου, so a reader may not move it; that he is listed here too is a second Greek day and is left in the report. **The Greek adds the whole story of the mission and no years at all**: the flight deeper into the desert when the crowds broke his stillness, the Theotokos appearing in a dream and commanding him to choose twelve and go to Iberia, the names written on separate papers and laid on the holy table, the night of prayer, the twelve papers an angel took from the altar into his hands before them all, the monk Euthymius left as abbot of the skete, the angel warning Bishop Eulogius of the Georgian capital of their coming, the bishop going out with clergy and people to meet them, the wonder like Pentecost by which John spoke Georgian, and their preaching through all Georgia and their veneration of the blessed places Saint Nina had passed, whom the page sends to 14 Ιανουαρίου. **No year, no hymn**, and the page does not say where any of the twelve settled afterwards — the sees and monasteries in their corpus names come from the Romanian side and nothing here is added to them. His head line is «Οσιος Ιωσηφ Μαθητης Του Οσιου Ιωαννη»; the page does not name Alaverdi or make him a bishop, so the folder's `hierarch` stands on the Romanian side alone and `types` is not touched.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 28.09.2026 (15. септембар ст. ст.) — „Св. Јосиф еп. Алавердски.“
